diagnostic_evidence.quote: G=-\left(\widehat{A}_{1}^{(k)}\right)^{-1}\left(A_{0}+A_{2}^{(k)} G^{2^k+1}\right)
By multiplying the first equation in \eqref{eq:crqme} to the right by $W_{G,1}$

issues.failure_explanation: With the recurrences eq:crgen and the QME eq:qme as defined in the paper, the four identities in eq:crqme are false: each needs one sign flipped (the correct forms are A_0^{(k)}-A_1^{(k)}G^{2^k}+A_2^{(k)}G^{2^{k+1}}=0, R^{2^{k+1}}A_0^{(k)}-R^{2^k}A_1^{(k)}+A_2^{(k)}=0, A_0+\widehat A_1^{(k)}G-A_2^{(k)}G^{2^k+1}=0, A_2+R\widehat A_1^{(k)}-R^{2^k+1}A_0^{(k)}=0). Scalar counterexample: A_0=-1, A_1=5/2, A_2=-1 (G=1/2 solves the QME); after one CR step A_0^{(1)}=2/5, A_1^{(1)}=17/10, A_2^{(1)}=2/5, \widehat A_1^{(1)}=21/10, and the first stated identity evaluates to 17/20\neq 0 (the sign-corrected version is exactly 0; algebraically A_0^{(1)}-A_1^{(1)}G^2+A_2^{(1)}G^4=-(A_0G+A_1G^2+A_2G^3)=0). The same sign-convention slip invalidates the two displayed recovery formulas for G and R, and makes the claim in the proof of prop:A0KW that the roots of a_k(z) are \lambda_i^{2^k} wrong (they are -\lambda_i^{2^k}), which is immaterial there since only moduli are used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of one term in each of the four identities of eq:crqme and in the two recovery formulas, and adjust the signs in the proofs that invoke them; all downstream statements are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated CR invariants, the recovery formulas following eq:crqme, and the premises used in the proof of prop:A0KW and in the derivation of eq:a0k and of S_G/S_R are wrong as printed; the conclusions all survive a mechanical sign correction because the downstream arguments are norm-based.
issues.title: CR invariance identities (eq:crqme) are false as stated (sign errors)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, mechanical sign correction verifiable by a one-line scalar check; every substantive claim, rate and guarantee survives with no new argument needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the eigenvalues of $S_2$, which are moved to 0, and the eigenvalues of $S_1^{-1}$, which are moved to infinity
\left(I_m+zX(S_1-zI_q)^{-1} U_1 \right)
Moreover, assume that $U_1 R=S_1^{-1} U_1$ and $G V_2= V_2S_2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis 'S_1^2 U_1 A_0 + S_1 U_1 A_1 + S_2 A_2=0' is dimensionally ill-formed (S_2 is q\times q, A_2 is m\times m, q<m), so the theorem relies on an undefined object. If repaired order-preservingly as ...+U_1A_2=0, the conclusion is false: for A(z)=diag((z-1)(z-4),(z-4)(z-8)) with q=1, S_1=1/4, U_1=e_2^\top, X=e_2, S_2=1, V_2=e_1, Y=e_1^\top (U_1X=YV_2=1) both hypotheses hold, but the (2,2) entry of the defined \widetilde A(z) equals (z-4)(z-8)/(1-4z), which has an uncanceled pole at z=1/4, so \widetilde A is not a polynomial. The reading consistent with th5 and with Section 3's application requires the hypothesis U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0 and the conclusion that the eigenvalues of S_1 (not S_1^{-1}) are moved to infinity; as printed the conclusion also misidentifies the moved eigenvalues, since eigenvalues of S_1^{-1} need not be eigenvalues of A(z) at all (same example with S_1=4: the eigenvalue moved to infinity is 4\in\sigma(S_1), while 1/4\notin\sigma(A)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate th3.2 with the dimensionally consistent, correctly ordered hypothesis U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0 and with 'the eigenvalues of S_1 moved to infinity' in the conclusion; Section 3's invocation then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The quoted deflation theorem underpinning Section 3 is unreliable as printed; the derivation of the \widetilde A_i coefficient formulas, of the factorization eq:facat, and hence the written justifications of prop:added-2 and thm:added-1 rest on it (their statements are correct under the repaired reading, but the proof route is unsound as written).
issues.title: Theorem th3.2 (block shift-and-deflate) is ill-formed and false as stated
issues.why_classification: The theorem as printed is false (not merely imprecise) under each single-token repair, and the correct statement must be reconstructed by cross-checking th5 and Section 3; but the repair is local and no downstream result is lost once the statement is corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with the convention that $1/\infty=0$ and $1/0=\infty$
The eigenvalues of $A(z)$ are $\lambda_1=0$, $\mu_j=\cos \frac{2\pi(j-1)}{3}+ i \sin \frac{2\pi(j-1)}{3} $, for $j=1,2,3$, each with multiplicity 2, and $\lambda_8=\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction applies th3.2 with S_1=\Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}, so the left factor of \widetilde A(z) contains (\Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}-zI_q)^{-1}, which is defined only when \Lambda_{R,1} is nonsingular, i.e. when all of \lambda_{m+\ell+1},\ldots,\lambda_{2m} are finite. The standing assumptions explicitly allow infinite eigenvalues (1/\infty=0 is listed among the eigenvalues of R), and the paper's own Example 1 has \lambda_8=\infty, so \sigma(\Lambda_{R,1})=\{0\} there: the factor, hence \widetilde A(z), the factorization eq:facat, and the derivation of the coefficient formulas and of the reduced equations are undefined exactly in a case the paper claims to cover and runs numerically. No alternative derivation avoiding \Lambda_{R,1}^{-1} (e.g. direct verification of the coefficient formulas, which do not involve the inverse) is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the unstated hypothesis that \Lambda_{R,1} is nonsingular (which excludes Example 1), or re-derive Section 3's identities (the \widetilde A_i coefficient formulas, the polynomiality/factorization claims and the eigenvalue counts) by a direct algebraic or limiting argument that avoids \Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the deflation step, of the \bar A_i structures, of the eigenvalue claims for \bar G and \bar R, and of the reduced QMEs is unavailable whenever \lambda_{2m}=\infty, a regime included in the assumptions and realized in Example 1; prop:added-2 and thm:added-1 are unproven there as written (their statements remain true and salvageable by direct algebra).
issues.title: Section 3 deflation construction is undefined when \Lambda_{R,1} is singular (e.g. Example 1)
issues.why_classification: A complete repair requires either a contained but nontrivial re-derivation of Section 3 without \Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}, or an added hypothesis that visibly narrows the advertised scope by excluding the paper's own Example 1; the final results themselves survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, in particular $\limsup_{k\to\infty}{\nullity(A_0^{(k)})}\ge m-\ell$.
the roots of \[a_k(z)=\det(A_0^{(k)}+z A_1^{(k)}+z^2 A_2^{(k)})\] are
\lambda_i^{2^k}, \quad \text{for} \quad k=1,\ldots,2m.
as $k \rightarrow \infty$,  $a_k(z)$ has exactly $m-\ell$ zeros that converge to 0, which implies that $\lim_{k\to\infty}{\nullity(A_0^{(k)})}= m-\ell$

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed limit of nullities fails whenever some of \lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{m-\ell} are nonzero (the generic case; e.g. Example 3, where \lambda_k=1/3+1/(\ell+k)\neq 0). By the CR root property invoked in the same proof, \det A_0^{(k)}=a_k(0) is, up to a nonzero factor, the product of the (\pm\lambda_i^{2^k}), hence nonzero when no \lambda_i equals 0; then A_0^{(k)} is nonsingular and nullity(A_0^{(k)})=0 for all k, not m-\ell. Both inferences in the proof are invalid: A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1}\to 0 does not produce any nullity at finite k (tiny singular values are not zeros), and roots of a_k converging to 0 are not roots at 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the nullity conclusion by the singular-value statement that the m-\ell smallest singular values of A_0^{(k)} (resp. A_2^{(k)}) decay with limsup rate at most |\lambda_{m-\ell}| (resp. 1/|\lambda_{m+\ell+1}|), which follows from the first part of the proof, and rephrase the subsequent rank-drop claims accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The 'Moreover' conclusion of prop:A0KW is false as stated, and the bridge from the proposition to the SVD-based extraction via an exact rank drop is unjustified in its nullity form; it must be reformulated via singular-value decay (which still leaves the subspace-convergence gap of eq:10-1).
issues.title: prop:A0KW's nullity conclusion is false
issues.why_classification: A stated conclusion of a labelled proposition is outright false in the generic regime and must be replaced by a weaker, different-type (rate-based) statement, with the downstream rank-drop argument reformulated; the proposition's main bounds survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, there exists a sequence of matrices $\{\widetilde{\Lambda}_{G,1}^{(k)}\}_k\in \mathbb{R}^{(m-l)\times (m-l)}$
$V_{0,2}^{(k)}$ approximates the invariant subspace of $G$ corresponding to the eigenvalues in the open unit disk

issues.failure_explanation: The claim that the trailing right singular subspace of A_0^{(k)} (and the corresponding block of U_2^{(k)} for R) converges to the invariant subspace of G (resp. R) is the linchpin of Algorithm alg:isg, yet no argument is given. prop:A0KW provides only \|A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1}\|\to 0 at rate |\lambda_{m-\ell}|^{2^k} (plus the false nullity statement); subspace convergence additionally requires a lower bound on the leading \ell singular values of A_0^{(k)} and a perturbation argument, neither of which is established under the stated (boundedness-only) hypotheses. The step is logically invalid in general: a matrix may have a tiny singular value in a direction orthogonal to the damped subspace (e.g. diag(\epsilon_k,0) with W_{G,1}=e_2 has null space spanned by e_1), so smallness of A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1} together with rank drop does not force V_{0,2}^{(k)} to align with span(W_{G,1}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the subspace convergence under the stated assumptions (or under an added spectral-gap/stability hypothesis) via a perturbation argument bounding the subspace angle by \|A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1}\|/\sigma_\ell(A_0^{(k)}) together with a uniform lower bound on the leading singular values.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence and correctness justification of Algorithm alg:isg, and hence of alg:gfull (BS-CR) - that the computed W_G, \Lambda_{G,1}, T_R, \Lambda_{R,1} approximate the required invariant subspaces - is unestablished; the advertised reliable convergence in the null-recurrent \ell>1 regime rests on this unproven step.
issues.title: Convergence of the SVD subspaces to the invariant subspaces (eq:10-1) is asserted without argument
issues.why_classification: The missing ingredient is a contained but genuinely nontrivial lemma (gap plus perturbation analysis), or an added hypothesis slightly narrowing scope; no global proof architecture is needed and the algorithmic results would survive with it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \textbf{Output:} the solution $\bar{G}_{11}$ of the QME \eqref{eq:qmeB} with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$.
with $Q$ and $Z$ unitary and $T$ and $S$ upper triangular
and $\bar{G}_{11}$ is the only solution to \eqref{eq:qmeGbar} with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$

issues.failure_explanation: The pencil (M,N) has all 2\ell eigenvalues on the unit circle (each \mu_i twice), so an arbitrary generalized Schur ordering does not place \mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell in the leading block; the algorithm never specifies the reordering/selection of the deflating subspace, and Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1} then yields whatever solution corresponds to the leading block (or is undefined if Z_{11} is singular), not the promised one. The identification moreover rests on the asserted but unproven claim that \bar G_{11} is the only solution of eq:qmeGbar with eigenvalues \mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell, which itself depends on the unproven remark that \ker A(\mu_i) is one-dimensional; with repeated unit-circle eigenvalues, different deflating subspaces generally give different solutions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit eigenvalue-selection/reordering step placing \mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell in the leading block of the generalized Schur form, and prove the uniqueness/identification of the reduced solution (via one-dimensionality of \ker A(\mu_i) and the deflating-subspace correspondence), or verify a posteriori that the computed solution has the required spectrum.
issues.overall_effect: alg:QZ's stated output is not guaranteed by its stated computation; since alg:gfull obtains \bar G_{11} (and then \bar R_{11}, \bar G_{21}, \bar R_{12}, and G, R) from it, the correctness of the BS-CR output is not established as specified.
issues.title: alg:QZ omits the deflating-subspace selection and rests on an unproven uniqueness claim
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a selection step plus a contained but nontrivial uniqueness argument; without them the algorithm's output contract fails, but no global redesign or loss of the method is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Compute $B_i$, $i=0,1,2$, by means of \eqref{eq:Bbar}.
by means of \eqref{G_final} and \eqref{R_final}, respectively.
If the matrix $\bar{A}_{122} \in \mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ is nonsingular, the systems \eqref{22} and \eqref{23} can be transformed into the QME

issues.failure_explanation: The step computing B_i by eq:Bbar requires \bar A_{122}^{-1} and is executed unconditionally, before the algorithm tests \bar A_{122} for nonsingularity; if \bar A_{122} is singular the B_i are undefined. Moreover, when the If-branch is skipped, \bar G_{21} and \bar R_{12} are never computed, yet the final step reconstructs G and R via eq:G_final/eq:R_final, which use \bar G_{21} (and \bar R_{12}). Nothing in the assumptions guarantees \bar A_{122} nonsingular, and no alternative (e.g. solving the coupled systems eq:22/eq:23 directly) is specified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Move the nonsingularity test before the computation of B_i and either make \bar A_{122} nonsingular an explicit input requirement with a failure exit, or specify a fallback such as solving the coupled systems eq:22 and eq:23 directly.
issues.overall_effect: alg:gfull (BS-CR) is not well defined on the part of its advertised input class where \bar A_{122} is singular: it attempts an undefined inversion and then an undefined reconstruction.
issues.title: alg:gfull is undefined when \bar A_{122} is singular (inversion precedes the check; no fallback)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local restructuring of the algorithm's guard plus an explicit input condition; the method, rates and scope on instances with nonsingular \bar A_{122} are unchanged, and the singular case was never established anyway.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, from the numerical experiments, the proposed approach is much more accurate than classical CR.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's own accuracy metric (the defined residual), Table tab:example1 reports 4.4e-16 for CR versus 3.9e-15 for BS-CR, so CR is slightly more accurate in Example 1; the sentence 'Concerning residual error, BS-CR is clearly the most accurate' is contradicted by the paper's own data, and the introduction's blanket claim that the approach is 'much more accurate than classical CR' is not supported by Example 1 (it is supported by Examples 2-3).

failure_location.quote: Concerning residual error, \texttt{BS-CR} is clearly the most accurate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sentence to match the table (e.g. BS-CR attains near machine precision in one iteration while CR needs 30 iterations and S-CR/FPI are less accurate) and qualify the introduction's accuracy claim accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: A stated numerical conclusion about Example 1 is false as written; the algorithms and theory are unaffected, but the comparative-accuracy claim for this experiment is unreliable.
issues.title: Example 1 text claims BS-CR is 'clearly the most accurate' but the table shows CR with a smaller residual
issues.why_classification: A local textual correction reconciles the claim with the reported data; no theorem, algorithm or guarantee is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has $\ell$ distinct roots $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ of modulus $1$, each with multiplicity 2
Moreover, $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ are eigenvalues of $A(z)$ of multiplicity 2.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 (\ell=8) the list \mu_1,\ldots,\mu_8 contains 1 twice and -1 twice, so A(z) has only 6 distinct unit-circle roots, with 1 and -1 of multiplicity 4 (each listed value appears once in G and once via R_{11}=G_{11}^{-1}); this violates the standing assumption of \ell distinct roots of modulus 1 each with multiplicity 2, and the claim that the \mu_i are eigenvalues of multiplicity 2 is false for the repeated values. The discussion asserts that the only deviation from the assumptions is the complex field, with the theory 'easily extended'; but repeated unit-circle roots are a structural deviation: the distinctness/multiplicity-2 structure underlies the (unproven) uniqueness of the reduced solution and the deflating-subspace selection, and is not covered by a complex-field extension.

failure_location.quote: However, the convergence theory developed in the paper can be easily extended to the complex case.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the duplicated values in Case 3 by eight distinct unit-modulus numbers (re-running the experiment), or state explicitly that Case 3 exceeds the distinctness assumption and that the theory does not cover repeated unit-circle roots.
issues.overall_effect: One of the three test cases lies outside the assumed framework as presented and the scope claim covering it is inaccurate; the theoretical results are unaffected, but Example 3 Case 3 does not instantiate the theory it is presented under.
issues.title: Example 3, Case 3 violates the distinctness assumption on the unit-circle eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local change to the example or an added caveat; no theorem or algorithm is invalidated, though the experiment's claimed coverage is withdrawn.
